categories.label: Risk Taxonomies and Multi-Stage Classification Frameworks
categories.memo: Studies that develop structured taxonomies or risk-factor lists spanning the full MMC/prefabrication lifecycle, providing the underlying classification schemes on which assessment and allocation are built.

codes.label: EPC/lifecycle risk category structures
codes.description: Frameworks that partition prefabricated project risk into discrete categories (design, procurement, construction, economic, policy, management) under EPC or similar integrated delivery arrangements.

codes.label: Modular/MiC critical risk-factor lists
codes.description: Ranked or catalogued lists of risk factors specific to modular construction (contractual disputes, transportation costs, sequencing, design changes, permitting) used to prioritize contractual attention.

codes.label: Supply chain risk network mapping
codes.description: Social-network-analysis-based identification of interconnected risk nodes across designer, contractor, manufacturer and client roles in prefabrication supply chains.

codes.label: Decision-criteria taxonomies for method selection risk
codes.description: Structured lists of factors (schedule, cost, logistics, regulation) that shape the risk profile of choosing modular/precast vs conventional methods, informing early contractual decisions.

categories.label: Quantitative and Decision-Support Risk Assessment Methodologies
categories.memo: Studies applying formal analytical techniques to weight, rank or simulate risk in MMC/prefabrication, informing how contracts might specify or reference risk evaluation processes.

codes.label: Grey-fuzzy and weighting-based risk evaluation
codes.description: Use of grey-fuzzy or weighted-scoring methods to determine relative significance of risk categories (e.g., construction risk weighted highest, policy risk lowest) in EPC prefabricated projects.

codes.label: Social network analysis of propagated risk
codes.description: SNA methods used to identify central, high-propagation risk nodes (e.g., poor resource/schedule estimation) within prefabrication supply chains, indicating where contractual risk allocation should concentrate.

codes.label: Simulation and game-theoretic payment allocation models
codes.description: Simulation-based and cooperative game-theory (e.g., Shapley value) approaches to quantify marginal contribution of parties to delay/bottleneck outcomes and translate this into differentiated contractual payment/penalty rules.

codes.label: Survey-based ranking and statistical risk-perception studies
codes.description: Structured surveys ranking risk factors' criticality to cost/schedule and testing for differences in risk perception across stakeholder groups, informing which risks contracts should explicitly address.

categories.label: Contractual Allocation of Risk Among Owner, Contractor, Manufacturer and Supplier
categories.memo: Studies examining how responsibility for MMC-specific risks should or does shift among parties compared with traditional delivery, including integrated delivery mechanisms and emerging digital contract tools.

codes.label: Consolidation of risk under integrated delivery (EPC/design-build)
codes.description: Shifting of design, procurement and construction risk onto a single general contractor or design-build entity to reduce fragmentation across prefabrication stages.

codes.label: Shared risk/reward structures under IPD
codes.description: Multiparty agreements with shared risk and reward, incentive/compensation mechanisms tied to cost savings, and proactive versus reactive risk management approaches.

sub_codes.label: Incentive and compensation clause design
sub_codes.description: Provisions linking cost savings to shared incentive payments, and risks of incomplete implementation by inexperienced parties.ID and description of ambiguous liability waivers.)

sub_codes.label: Liability waiver and insurance allocation
sub_codes.description: Contractual clauses on limitation of liability, insurance consultant requirements, and coverage duration that differ across standard IPD forms.

codes.label: Smart-contract-based dynamic risk/reward allocation
codes.description: Automated allocation of payments and penalties among fabricator, crane operator and installation crew based on quantified marginal contribution to delay, including adaptation to external conditions like weather.

codes.label: Fabricator scope and interference limitation clauses
codes.description: Contractual allocation giving module fabricators expanded procurement/manufacturing scope and minimal owner/contractor interference once selected, particularly where schedule is critical.

codes.label: Developer transaction cost and coordination risk allocation
codes.description: Allocation of hidden transaction costs (from design changes, new technology adoption) to developers, and the developer's coordinating role in managing multi-party cost risk in prefabricated concrete (PC) projects.

categories.label: Design-Stage Risk and Change Control
categories.memo: Risks arising from insufficient design development, late design changes, and the tension between early design freeze and flexibility in MMC projects, with implications for contractual change-order provisions.

codes.label: Insufficient design depth and cross-disciplinary coordination risk
codes.description: Errors and omissions in precast component design arising from inadequate detailed/in-depth design and lack of close cooperation among professionals.

codes.label: Early design freeze as contractual necessity
codes.description: Requirement to freeze specifications and concept/detailed design early because late changes are costly, risky and schedule-sensitive once modules are in fabrication, creating tension between certainty and flexibility.

codes.label: Late design change propagation risk
codes.description: Downstream cost and schedule impacts when client- or designer-originated design changes occur after fabrication has begun, propagating through assembly and installation.

codes.label: Design risk allocation shift from engineering-design to engineering-construction
codes.description: Recognition that modularisation changes where design-related risk resides, requiring increased upfront engineering effort including design-for-transportation.

categories.label: Manufacturing, Procurement and Quality Compliance Risk
categories.memo: Risks and contractual mechanisms concerning component quality, certification, traceability and regulatory compliance across the manufacturing and procurement stages of off-site construction.

codes.label: Quality defects and self-certification limitations
codes.description: Reliance on manufacturer self-certification as insufficient alone to guarantee compliance, necessitating supplementary third-party certification and traceability measures.

codes.label: Chain of custody and traceability obligations
codes.description: Contractual/regulatory requirement for a chain of custody approach and technologies (RFID, GPS, barcodes) enabling tracking of components from manufacture to installation.

codes.label: Regulatory fragmentation and liability ambiguity across jurisdictions
codes.description: Inconsistent interpretation of code compliance by local authorities and liability exposure for authorities when modular components are inadequately scrutinized, motivating standardized registers or task forces.

codes.label: Government standards, mandates and incentive risk
codes.description: Effects of regulatory instruments—mandatory assembly rate minimums, lack of comprehensive standards, tax incentives/subsidies—on developer risk and market entry for prefabricated construction.

codes.label: Procurement-stage transport and handling damage risk
codes.description: Quality defects and damage to precast components arising from inadequate protective measures and incorrect placement during transport, and the intersection of procurement and design decisions.

categories.label: Transportation and Logistics Risk
categories.memo: Risks specific to moving prefabricated modules/components from factory to site, including regulatory, cost and site-access constraints that affect contractual planning and responsibility.

codes.label: Module/component transport damage and delay risk
codes.description: Physical damage, loss, or delay of modules/precast components during transit due to size, weight, handling and cross-border/customs processes.

codes.label: Site access, crane and staging constraints
codes.description: Logistical barriers such as limited site access, storage constraints, crane availability and traffic control requirements in dense urban or high-rise modular projects.

codes.label: Cost and capacity constraints on transportation
codes.description: Additional design/engineering effort and structural material required specifically for transportation, and manufacturing/logistics capacity limitations constraining delivery.

categories.label: On-Site Construction and Installation Risk
categories.memo: Risks arising during erection, hoisting, and interface assembly of prefabricated components on site, and how synchronization between offsite and onsite work should be contractually managed.

codes.label: Temporary support and hoisting equipment risk
codes.description: Instability of temporary support systems and machinery selection during hoisting identified as the most significant construction-stage risk in prefabricated EPC projects.

codes.label: Interface and tolerance management between modules
codes.description: Technical/contractual risk from tight-tolerance interfaces between modules and on-site elements, requiring predefined tolerance requirements and skilled manufacturers.

codes.label: Offsite-onsite schedule synchronization risk
codes.description: Need to synchronize factory production scheduling with on-site construction sequencing to avoid bottlenecks, out-of-sequence delivery, and propagated delay.

codes.label: Skilled labour and workmanship shortage risk
codes.description: Shortage of experienced modular construction professionals and skilled labour leading to quality problems and improper implementation on site.

categories.label: Economic, Financial and Market Risk Allocation
categories.memo: Studies addressing how cost overrun, payment, financing and market-based risks are distributed among parties in MMC/prefabrication projects, and how this shapes contractual risk-bearing.

codes.label: Contractor-borne cost overrun and payment delay risk
codes.description: Amplified economic risk to contractors under EPC where developers may delay payment or force price reductions despite higher baseline prefabrication costs.

codes.label: Financing and lender risk in modular/prefabrication markets
codes.description: Elevated lending risk due to high upfront capital costs and manufacturer solvency concerns, and the underexplored role of insurance/lending institutions in guaranteeing quality.

codes.label: Developer hidden transaction cost risk
codes.description: Additional hidden costs borne by developers from new technology adoption and management processes, exacerbated by design changes and reputational effects.

codes.label: Cost perception and stakeholder conflict over method selection
codes.description: Divergent stakeholder cost priorities (client cost focus vs contractor reluctance toward upfront prefabrication premiums) complicating risk-informed method selection decisions.

categories.label: Coordination, Communication and Interface Management as Risk Mitigation
categories.memo: Studies identifying coordination and communication mechanisms—interface management, integration, early involvement—as core strategies for mitigating risks distinctive to MMC/prefabrication, relevant to how contracts should structure collaboration obligations.

codes.label: Interface management as formal risk mitigation strategy
codes.description: Adoption of interface management practices to coordinate multiple parties and reduce complexity-driven risk in EPC prefabricated projects.

codes.label: Early stakeholder/fabricator involvement
codes.description: Early involvement of contractors, fabricators and manufacturers in design decision-making to avoid risky late-stage design gaps and to enable design standardization.

codes.label: Communication protocol and information-flow risk
codes.description: Outdated or informal communication practices (email, hard copies) between designer, contractor and manufacturer identified as a root cause of costly design-change and delivery risks, implying need for contractual data-sharing/BIM protocols.

codes.label: Multi-project resource contention risk
codes.description: Manufacturers serving multiple clients simultaneously causing resource coordination risk that spills over into individual project supply chains, a risk not typically addressed in bilateral contracts.
